clue.text: Sort mail out for preacher

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the first two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told to sort out the post on behalf of a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal, rearranging the letters of SORT and MAIL together.
explanation.definitionFit: A moralist lectures others on right conduct, as a preacher does from the pulpit.

clue.text: Complaint of boy stuck in tree

indicators.note: stuck in places the boy inside the tree

parts.note: may is hawthorn, a tree
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy has climbed a tree and got stuck, a familiar complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: MAY is another name for the hawthorn tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an illness, as is a malady.

clue.text: Being cracked, I have enlisted in the navy

indicators.note: enlisting in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A man joining the navy confesses he is cracking up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' is a link to the definition; 'enlisted in' is the container signal, borrowed from joining up.
explanation.definitionFit: Riven means split apart, so cracked is a synonym.

clue.text: Glowing, hit repeatedly and forced into shape

parts.note: to lam is to beat or thrash
bent means pushed out of straight into a curve

explanation.surface: Red-hot metal is beaten and bent into shape by a smith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link between the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambent describes a soft, flickering glow, as of a flame.

clue.text: Avoid making decision to pin down criminal

parts.note: to sit on someone is to hold them down
a fence is a criminal who receives stolen goods

explanation.surface: Someone dithers over whether to restrain a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: A fence is a receiver of stolen goods; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit on the fence is an idiom for refusing to take sides.

clue.text: People following a copper show perspicacity

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the people are placed after the copper

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
men means people in general

explanation.surface: A group walking behind a policeman shows good judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal; 'show' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name sharp insight and shrewd judgement; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Where fights take place, in the main

definitions.meaning: a pit for cockfights, so any arena of conflict
on a ship at sea (the main), the space where the helmsman stands or junior officers berthed

explanation.surface: Somewhere brawls happen, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' looks like 'mostly' but means at sea: the main is the open ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockpit is a pit for cockfighting and also a sunken steering area or compartment on a ship.

clue.text: Admitting pointed remark to artist spoils end of carnival

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the spoiling word takes the others inside

parts.note: mars means spoils
a dig is a cutting remark
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A barbed comment to a painter ruins the last night of the festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admitting' is the container signal and 'to' a link; Mardi Gras is the climax that ends carnival.
explanation.definitionFit: Mardi Gras, Shrove Tuesday, is the final day of the carnival season before Lent.

clue.text: Gas not initially very harmful for the very young

parts.note: neon is a gas

indicators.note: not initially means without its first letter

parts.note: fatal means deadly, so very harmful

explanation.surface: A gas is not, at first, very dangerous to babies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially' drops F from FATAL to leave ATAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Neonatal means relating to newborn babies.

clue.text: No score draw? This is not just a convenient arrangement

definitions.text: This is not just a convenient arrangement

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring
a draw is a contest in which the sides end level, so a game or match

explanation.surface: A goalless game is contrasted with a marriage of convenience.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage made for love is the opposite of an arranged marriage of convenience.

clue.text: Hopelessly out-of-date form of transport

definitions.meaning: an adjective for something hopelessly old-fashioned
a light carriage pulled by a horse

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned transport is described.
explanation.definitionFit: The horse-drawn carriage became a byword for anything outdated, after cars replaced it.

clue.text: Goods travel on road vehicle

indicators.note: in a down-the-page sense, one piece placed after another; here travel comes after the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a road vehicle
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: Merchandise moves along the road in a lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo is the freight or goods carried by a ship, plane or vehicle.

clue.text: Debt collector has gone astray, resulting in prison

parts.note: a dun is one who demands payment of a debt

indicators.note: gone astray means wandered off course, so the letters of gone are scrambled

explanation.surface: A bailiff has wandered off course and ended up in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' rearranges the letters of 'gone'; 'has' and 'resulting in' are links. A dun is an old word for a debt collector.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is an underground cell, a kind of prison.

clue.text: Pile car up -—- get another the same

indicators.note: up here means in a mess or disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: After piling up a car in a crash, the driver buys an identical one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' rearranges the letters of PILE CAR; 'get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica is an exact copy, another object identical to the first.

clue.text: Understand soldiers are in reserve, where they can be served by hospital, say

definitions.text: where they can be served by hospital, say

parts.note: to catch means to grasp or understand
men are soldiers in the ranks

indicators.note: the word are sits inside the reserve forces

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
taken as written

explanation.surface: Grasp that soldiers belong to the reserves, in the district a military hospital serves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's part-time army reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchment area is the district whose residents a hospital or school serves.

clue.text: Uncompromising chat with tutor foundering

indicators.note: foundering means collapsing or going wrong, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A conversation with a teacher is going badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foundering' rearranges CHAT and TUTOR; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutthroat competition is ruthless and uncompromising.

clue.text: Slightly shortened rectangle, about four by one, being forgotten

indicators.note: about means round, so the trimmed shape goes round the numbers
slightly shortened means losing just its last letter

parts.note: an oblong is a rectangle
IV is four in Roman numerals
I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A rectangle is trimmed a little and measured about four by one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slightly shortened' removes the last letter; 'about' is the container signal and 'by' joins the two numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblivion is the state of being forgotten.

clue.text: Heavy drinkers about to speak to fellow who keeps spilling things

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the drinkers go round the next pieces

parts.note: bingers drink to excess
to utter is to speak

explanation.surface: Boozers are about to talk to a clumsy man who keeps knocking drinks over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to speak' reads as 'on the point of speaking', but 'about' is the container signal and 'to' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterfingers is a jokey name for a clumsy person who drops or spills things.

clue.text: Seamen's knots all together

indicators.note: knots means tangles, so the letters are twisted together

explanation.surface: Sailors tie their knots as one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knots' rearranges all the letters of SEAMEN'S, the S included.
explanation.definitionFit: En masse is French for in a body, all together.

clue.text: Former spouse's allegation that -can make you cry

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse; the 's means has
a claim is an allegation

explanation.surface: A former partner's accusations can reduce you to tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cry' looks like weeping, but means call out; 'that can make you' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to cry out suddenly.

clue.text: Mythical creature seen to proceed slowly

definitions.meaning: a fire-breathing winged beast of legend

explanation.surface: A legendary beast is seen moving slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragon is a fabled beast, and to drag on is to go on slowly.

clue.text: Beastly smell in almost empty container

indicators.note: in signals one piece sitting within another
container signals that the trimmed word holds the smell inside it
almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: inane means empty or vacuous
hum is slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: A dreadful smell lingers in a nearly empty bin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the last letter; 'in' and 'container' signal the insertion. Hum is British slang for a stink.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean cruel and brutish, lacking human kindness; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Shield back of mother deer and young as they retreat

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the whole run of pieces is read right to left
the back of a word is its last letter

parts.note: an elk is a large deer
a cub is a young animal

explanation.surface: A mother deer and her fawn protect their rear as they withdraw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back of' takes R from mother; 'as they retreat' turns R + ELK + CUB into BUCKLER. 'Buck' and 'deer' tempt, but BUCK comes from the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A buckler is a small round shield held by a handle.

clue.text: One apprehended by fat landowner

indicators.note: apprehended by means caught and held, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: lard is pig fat
I is one

explanation.surface: Someone is arrested by a portly estate owner.
explanation.walkthrough: A laird is a Scottish landowner.
explanation.definitionFit: Laird is the Scots word for the owner of a landed estate.

clue.text: Clubs in which one is restrained

definitions.meaning: a prisoner held in fetters is said to be in these

explanation.surface: Golf clubs and shackles share a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Irons are both metal-headed golf clubs and the chains or fetters used to restrain prisoners.

clue.text: English mad on art

parts.note: raving means mad

explanation.surface: An Englishman is wildly enthusiastic about art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link here, between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Engraving, cutting designs into metal or wood for printing, is a graphic art.

clue.text: Indefinite number added to a number that's lower

indicators.note: added to places one piece directly before the other

parts.note: n stands for an indefinite number in maths
read as numb-er, something that numbs, such as the anaesthetic ether

explanation.surface: Arithmetic: adding an unknown to a number gives something smaller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a number' is not a figure but a 'numb-er', an anaesthetic such as ETHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Nether is an old word for lower, as in nether regions.

clue.text: Henchman demonstrating my right to a place in the field

parts.note: taken as written
mid-on is a cricket fielding position

explanation.surface: A loyal follower claims his right to a spot on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: MID-ON is a fielding position in cricket, near the bowler on the leg side; 'demonstrating' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrmidons were Achilles' loyal followers, so the word means an unquestioning henchman.
